items.title: Serian records hazardous API reading
items.summary: KUCHING: Serian recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 8am today. Meanwhile, three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (300), Kuching (291) and Sri Aman (214). An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 indicates moderate air quality, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.

items.title: Serian tops hazardous API chart at 364, multiple Sarawak districts suffer worsening air
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 30 — Serian recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 8am today. Meanwhile, three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (300), Kuching (291) and Sri Aman (214). Areas recording unhealthy API readings include Sarikei (195), Sibu (187), Bintulu (179), Samalaju (171), Mukah (170), Kapit (159), Miri (155) and the Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (151).

items.title: Merdeka spirit opens new path for 17-year-old TVET hopeful
items.summary: Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said his two adopted children, Gabriel Ooi and Sandira, helped the girl, Nabila, resume her education after she was forced to leave school when her mother fell ill and lost her income. "Although Ooi and Sandira are of different races and religions, they stepped forward to help Nabila. Sim said the story began two weeks ago when Ooi sent him a brief WhatsApp message asking for help.

items.title: Third victim found near two others in Kota Kinabalu fire
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The third victim who went missing in a fire that destroyed about 200 water village homes in Numbak here was found by firefighters today. Acting Kota Kinabalu Fire and Rescue Station chief, Senior Assistant Fire Superintendent Mohd Hannis Moktar, when contacted, confirmed the discovery of the third victim. "The third victim was found not far from the location where the first two victims were found," he said.

items.title: #NSTViral: Malaysians head to southern Thailand despite boycott calls, travel advisory
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians continued crossing into southern Thailand for the Merdeka Day long weekend, despite recent boycott calls and travel advisories over traffic enforcement and security concerns. Videos and photographs shared on social media on Friday showed long queues at border checkpoints in Perlis and Kedah, with congestion particularly heavy at Padang Besar. TikTok user Amirul Guider shared a video showing vehicles backed up at the Padang Besar border checkpoint about 7am yesterday.

items.title: Early morning fire in Kota Kinabalu squatter area, 39 personnel deployed to contain blaze
items.summary: The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), in a statement, said it received an emergency call at 1.40am, following which firefighters were deployed and arrived at the scene, located 18 kilometres away, at 1.58am. “A total of 39 personnel from the Kota Kinabalu, Lintas and Penampang Fire and Rescue Stations (BBP) were deployed to the scene to carry out firefighting operations,” it said. According to the Sabah JBPM, firefighters were battling the blaze using two streams and four water jets, with water supplied by fire engines.

items.title: Iceland in suspense after close EU vote
items.summary: REYKJAVIK: Iceland voted Saturday in a referendum on whether to resume membership negotiations with the European Union, with a close race predicted and the final result expected late in the night or the next morning. Voting stations closed at 10pm (2200 GMT). On Saturday, Iceland's 273,000 voters were asked to answer 'Yes' or 'No' to the question: "Should Iceland resume accession negotiations with the European Union?"

items.title: Two found charred, one missing in fire that destroys 200 homes in Kota Kinabalu
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Two people were found charred while another remained missing after a fire destroyed about 200 homes in Numbak here early today. Acting Kota Kinabalu Fire and Rescue Station chief, Senior Assistant Fire Superintendent Mohd Hannis Moktar, said two victims were found by firefighters during the firefighting operation. "The fire involved non-permanent water village houses across three villages — Kampung Lok Buta, Kampung Lok Poring and Kampung Sabang Lama.

items.title: UPTM helps Pos Kemar youth chart brighter future
items.summary: GERIK: Education is key to transforming lives and giving the Orang Asli younger generation in Pos Kemar a chance at a better future. Through the Mara Prihatin—Jejak Aspirasi UPTM @ Pos Kemar programme, Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia (UPTM) students took learning beyond the classroom, engaging directly with children and students in the community. UPTM vice-chancellor Prof Dr Sharifah Syahirah Sy Shiekh said the programme gave UPTM students an opportunity to give back to the community while gaining knowledge and first-hand experience of the Orang Asli community.

items.title: Media Prima celebrates Malaysian spirit through 'Wajah Malaysia' campaign
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Everyday Malaysians will take centre stage in Media Prima Bhd's campaign celebrating the resilience, compassion and diversity that shape the country's shared identity. The "Wajah Malaysia: Nadi Negara, Cerita Kita" campaign will feature digital initiatives and community activities for National Day and Malaysia Day. The completed mosaic will be unveiled across Media Prima's platforms and digital screens on Malaysia Day on Sept 16.

items.title: The missing in Nepal-Tibet flash floods
items.summary: Nepal's disaster agency on Friday said 517 foreigners – which could include tourists as well as foreign workers – were still missing. Nepal The Nepal Tourism Board figures on Friday said 149 Nepali tourists were among the 622 it listed as missing. The Nepal Tourism Board said eight Chinese were unaccounted for, but 16 had been rescued.

items.title: Defence sec-gen takes first flight in Su-30MKM ahead of National Day flypast
items.summary: "The experience also offered an understanding of the capabilities required to keep strategic assets at a high state of readiness. He said this at the flypast rehearsal at Subang air base yesterday. Lokman said the aircraft continued to play an important role, particularly in protecting the country's airspace and maritime interests.

items.title: Govt reviewing egg prices, says minister
items.summary: SERDANG: The government is reviewing rising egg prices following concerns from producers about high operating costs and mounting industry pressures, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. He said his ministry and the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry had met industry players to find out what was causing egg prices to spike. Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Egg Merchants Association chairman Low Hin Ching said retail egg prices had risen five times over the past three weeks due to lower yields caused by poor-quality feed and hot weather.

items.title: 'This is all we know': Farmer fears 40-year-old poultry business may end
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Desmond is facing a dilemma over the two poultry farms he inherited from his father, one that could bring an end to the 40-year-old family business. Desmond said flies had always been present, although the growth of residential areas had worsened the problem. He said flies at poultry farms, especially open farms like his, were unavoidable, although their population could be managed with traps, pesticides and proper sanitation.

items.title: Chicken, egg prices rise as poultry farms face mounting pressures [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Chicken and egg prices are rising as poultry farms face closure amid fly infestations, labour shortages, rising feed costs and regulatory pressure, industry players said. The Federation of Livestock Farmers' Associations of Malaysia said farms could meet domestic demand, but market supply had become "very tight" amid industry strain. The sources said open farms, relying on natural airflow for ventilation, were the most affected.

items.title: Israel army says struck Hamas commander in Gaza hospital compound
items.summary: GAZA CITY: Israel's military said it struck a Hamas commander within the compound of a Gaza hospital on Saturday, while the territory's health officials said Israeli strikes elsewhere killed four people. Israeli fire east of Deir al-Balah killed one person, the agency said. The Israeli military said it was checking the reports.

items.title: Getting the dogs, horses ready for Merdeka Day parade [WATCH]
items.summary: Twenty-five dogs from the armed forces' Military Dog Wing or "Wolf Wing" and 25 horses from the army's Ceremonial Cavalry Squadron will take part in the parade. With the canine and mounted contingents nearing the final stages of preparation, the handlers said the animals were ready to take centre stage alongside their human counterparts tomorrow. Wolf Wing assistant head Captain Duin Tat said the K9 contingent, comprising 25 handlers and 25 dogs, had undergone about a month of preparation at the Army Combat Training Centre in Johor before arriving here for final rehearsals.

items.title: Norway's King Haakon VIII pays tribute to late father in first speech
items.summary: OSLO: Norway's new King Haakon VIII on Saturday addressed Norwegians for the first time since taking the throne, paying tribute to his 89-year-old father who died the day before. "Above all, you were a person who remained committed to your values and dedicated to your duties," Haakon said of the late King Harald V in a televised speech. Be ourselves," Haakon said of his father.

items.title: Peeling back the past: Secrets uncovered at KL's heritage sites
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sometimes, the clues to a building's past are hiding in plain sight. At Muzium Diraja Kuala Lumpur, a restoration team uncovered a double-layer roof and other construction features that differed from conventional Malaysian building methods. At Seri Negara, peeling back layers of paint revealed an original duck egg green colour, while an old staircase was found buried beneath a pathway.

items.title: N. Korea defence minister dismissed
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea's defence minister has been dismissed as part of a reshuffle of the country's military leadership, state media reported Sunday. The "structural reorganisation plans" were decided during a meeting on Saturday led by Kim Jong Un, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. Kim Song Gi, director of the General Political Bureau of the Korean People's Army, was named as the new defence minister.

items.title: Inside the painstaking restoration of Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: To bring a 129-year-old landmark back to life, the team restoring Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad (BSAS) first had to step back in time. Old photographs helped the team recreate the original form of the clock tower dome, while restoration and hacking works uncovered features hidden for decades, including staircases buried beneath the building. It was part construction, part detective work.

items.title: Beyond monuments and textbooks, KL’s Statesman Memorial guards Malaysia’s nation‑building story
items.summary: One such place is the Statesman Memorial (also known as Memorial Negarawan), housed in the former Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) along Jalan Dato Onn, which bears witness to the country’s post-independence administrative history. National Archives of Malaysia (ANM) director-general Zaidin Mohd Noor said the building’s historical significance lies not merely in its role as an administrative office, but as a physical witness to Malaysia’s journey in governance and development. — Picture by Yusof Isa The former Prime Minister’s Office housed the tenures of Tun Abdul Razak Hussein, Tun Hussein Onn and Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad — who occupied the office for the longest period, 22 years — until the federal government administrative centre moved to Putrajaya in 2003.

items.title: No Dutch investigation into Mladic's death
items.summary: THE HAGUE: A UN court said Saturday evening that Dutch authorities would not be conducting a criminal investigation into the death of Ratko Mladic, the convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal. Mladic, who was serving life in prison in The Hague for genocide and war crimes committed during the 1992-1995 Bosnian war, died in hospital on Thursday after suffering several strokes in recent months. The International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals said Dutch authorities had carried out the procedures required by national law.

items.title: Seven AUKU sections on student freedoms to get priority, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Seven sections of the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU) relating to students, including provisions on freedom, will be given priority in the process of repealing the Act, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir. He said seven of AUKU's 44 sections relate to students, while the rest cover matters including the establishment, administration and governance of universities. "AUKU is the parent Act of universities, the main one for the establishment of a university.

items.title: 91 Malaysians remain uncontactable after Nepal, China floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 91 Malaysians, comprising 55 in Nepal and 36 in China, remain uncontactable as of 8pm today following floods that struck on Aug 26, the Foreign Ministry said. "The ministry understands the heightened concern regarding the limited personal information released publicly on individual Malaysians who remain uncontactable," it said. The ministry said personal details would not be released publicly without the consent of the immediate next of kin.

items.title: 23.4pct of KL children under 5 stunted, says Health Minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malnutrition among children under 5 in the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur is worrying, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. He said National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) data showed that 23.4 per cent of children in Kuala Lumpur were stunted, while 12.4 per cent were underweight, 8.1 per cent affected by wasting and 7.5 per cent overweight. He said the Health Ministry was taking a proactive approach by going into communities to identify at-risk children who did not regularly attend health facilities.

items.title: Man died from injuries sustained in fall from height at Desa ParkCity, say police
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The post-mortem on the male suspect believed to have fallen from a condominium in Desa ParkCity, Kepong, on Thursday was completed this evening at the National Institute of Forensic Medicine, Hospital Kuala Lumpur. City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the findings revealed that the 48-year-old man's cause of death was multiple injuries consistent with a fall from a height. Earlier, the media reported that the man's wife and two children, who were found dead inside a unit at the same condominium, had died from stab wounds.

items.title: Queen graces UTM royal gala dinner 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia graced the Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) Royal Gala Dinner 2026 tonight. UTM Pro-Chancellor Che Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Johor also graced the biennial event, which was also attended by UTM Pro-Chancellor Tan Sri Datuk Professor Emeritus Dr Mohd Zulkifli Mohd Ghazali and Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Shikata Noriyuki. "To date, UTM has awarded 1,013 Endowment Scholarships to B40 students.

items.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to 675
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Devastating floods near the border with China this week have killed at least 675 people in Nepal, the Himalayan nation's disaster authority said on Saturday. Chinese state media earlier confirmed seven dead in Tibet following Wednesday's disaster, taking the total killed to 682. The number of missing also includes 45 Nepali Army soldiers, 40 police officers, and 19 immigration and customs officers.

items.title: Men head to cosmetic clinics to complete weight-loss transformations
items.summary: AS top-selling weight-loss drugs help more men in the United States slim down, a growing number are seeking cosmetic treatments for sagging skin, hair loss and dental issues to complete their physical transformation, patients and plastic surgeons say. Reuters spoke to six male patients and a dozen cosmetic surgeons who said weight-loss drugs, social media and changing perceptions of masculinity are sending more men to clinics that offer such procedures. "I've seen probably a doubling in the number of male patients that I treat over the last one to two years," said Sean Alemi, Mark's doctor and a New York-based facial plastic surgeon.

items.title: Gulf expats hunker down between bouts of war
items.summary: SIX months into the Middle East war, the army of foreign workers and expatriates in the Gulf has largely stayed put — hoping to ride out the uncertainty caused by conflict rather than return to dim prospects back home. But the war, which has killed 41 people in the Gulf, has proven to be incredibly disruptive for many. "Dubai is the place to be, to be secure, to hustle, to make money, to save — and that opportunity is not provided back home," she said.

items.title: NST Leader: Stop love scammers — they are wanted for murder
items.summary: Romance scammers exploit something more powerful than greed: loneliness, trust, affection and the human desire for companionship. Once emotional dependence is established, victims can become remarkably resistant to warnings from family and friends. Strong family and social ties can make people feel less isolated and ready to seek advice either from the family or social circles when they encounter strangers.

items.title: As cyber threats strike at AI speed, Malaysia urged to embed risk‑based defence
items.summary: Telekom Malaysia Chief Information Security Officer Raja Azrina Raja Othman, who was among the co-founders of MyCERT in 1997, said cyber threats three decades ago were largely confined to specific systems and networks. Today, however, almost all services operate digitally and are interconnected, ranging from banking and government services to corporate operations and national critical infrastructure. “Cyber attackers today operate rapidly with the aid of AI.

items.title: Immigration to seek Thai details on syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia into Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Immigration Department will work with Thai authorities to obtain detailed information on an alleged syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia to Malaysia. “We will get further information from Thai authorities on this matter,” he said when contacted by Bernama today, after Thai media outlets reported that Thai authorities arrested two individuals suspected of being masterminds of a ring trafficking China nationals from the Cambodian border to Malaysia through Thailand. Thai authorities also identified four Thai nationals believed to be involved in the ring, including the individual arranging the immigrants’ journey from the Cambodia-Thai border to Hat Yai and onwards through to Malaysia.

items.title: Anwar: ‘Not a zero‑sum game’ as language mastery broadens unity and opportunity
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH, Aug 29 — Efforts to uphold Malay, the country’s official language, should not be seen as an attempt to undermine proficiency in other languages, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said every citizen, regardless of racial background, should have a good command of the national language, while at the same time, proficiency in other languages such as English, Mandarin and Tamil should continue to be strengthened to broaden educational and economic opportunities. Elaborating, Anwar said proficiency in Mandarin was becoming increasingly important given its position as one of the region’s major economic languages, while Malaysians were also interested in improving their proficiency in Tamil.

items.title: Anwar extends Malaysia’s condolences to Norway on passing of King Harald V
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today extended condolences on behalf of the Malaysian government to the people of Norway on the passing of King Harald V. Anwar said King Harald would be remembered for his generous understanding of what it meant to be Norwegian, including his recognition of the country’s diverse society. Anwar said King Harald also understood the weight of an oath and the importance of remaining true to one’s commitments. “Malaysia joins the people of Norway in mourning his passing,” the Prime Minister said.

items.title: Subang Jaya police open investigation into viral Facebook claim against officers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Police have opened an investigation paper regarding a Facebook post that allegedly contained defamatory statements against police officers at a petrol station in Batu 14, Puchong, Selangor yesterday. Subang Jaya district police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said his department received a report from a police officer who was on duty at the time of the incident at 10.54pm. “The police have opened an investigation paper following the allegations under Section 500 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

items.title: MAHA Expo hall closed after smoke incident, visitors evacuated as safety checks carried out
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 29 — Exhibition Hall A (Hall A) at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS) was temporarily closed today following a minor incident involving smoke and an unpleasant odour at 4.50pm. “To ensure the safety and comfort of everyone, members of the public and exhibitors in Hall A are advised to calmly evacuate the hall with immediate effect until further notice,” it said. It said Hall A would only be reopened after the authorities had confirmed that it was safe, adding that the safety of visitors, exhibitors and personnel remained the organisers’ top priority.

items.title: GRS to lead seat talks, Hajiji says coalition preparing machinery ahead of GE16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 29 — Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS), as the coalition leading the Sabah government, will take the lead in determining seat allocations with its government allies for the next general election, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. Hajiji, who is also Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah (PGRS) president, said the coalition would eventually discuss the distribution of parliamentary seats with parties currently in the state government, including Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Barisan Nasional (BN). Hajiji said the main consideration would be to field candidates capable of winning the election.

items.title: Anwar: Colonial‑era laws curbing student freedom must be abolished to realise true independence
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH, Aug 29 — Colonial-era laws restricting students’ freedom should be abolished to allow the true meaning of independence to be fully realised, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said university students should have more freedom to voice their views and take part in activities, as they would play a key role in shaping the country’s future. “That is why I announced last week that we would abolish university laws that restrict student activities.

items.title: Traffic crawls along 20km stretch entering Kelantan as school break and National Day surge builds
items.summary: Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said traffic police personnel and the Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit have been deployed to the location to conduct regular patrols. “Police are closely monitoring traffic flow along all major routes to ensure the safety and smooth movement of road users. However, he said traffic flow returned to normal after passing the diversion area.

items.title: Air quality worsens, two Sarawak stations breach very unhealthy levels, 29 areas nationwide unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Two monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, while 29 other areas nationwide registered unhealthy air quality. An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy), and above 300 (hazardous). API figures are updated hourly based on readings from 68 monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: ‘We can only pray’: Family of missing Malaysian in Nepal tragedy anxiously awaits news
items.summary: Mures, 40, said his father’s journey to perform a religious ceremony on Mount Kailash, Tibet turned into a terrifying nightmare for the family after he was last seen active on the WhatsApp application on the morning of the incident. “My father alone joined a group with 16 other Malaysians to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China to perform a religious ceremony. He said the family had contacted various parties to obtain the latest information including the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu and the police.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain in six states and KL until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has warned of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in seven states and Kuala Lumpur until 7pm today. MetMalaysia said the warning was issued for the entire state of Kelantan and 11 districts in Perak: Batang Padang, Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, Larut Matang, Selama, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk. The warning also covers Hulu Terengganu, Dungun, Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang in Terengganu, and Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Rompin, Raub, Bentong, Jerantut and Temerloh in Pahang.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia’s success must be anchored by a knowledgeable, disciplined generation
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Aug 29 — A country’s success should not be measured solely by economic and technological progress, but must also be supported by the development of a knowledgeable and disciplined younger generation, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The Prime Minister said young people should be provided with an education that also instils values, a spirit of service and a sense of responsibility towards their families, society and country. Also present were Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow and Chief Scout Datuk Prof Dr Mohd Zin Bidin.

items.title: Desa ParkCity family tragedy takes new turn as police reveal illegal investment issue alongside alleged love scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Police investigating the deaths of a family of four at a Desa ParkCity condominium in Kepong have revealed that the couple had also become entangled in an illegal investment scheme, adding a new dimension to a case already linked to an alleged love scam and RM260,000 in losses and debt. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said relatives of the couple were aware of both issues. “The family knew about the love scam problem and that they had become trapped in an illegal investment scheme.

items.title: Wisma Putra: 55 Malaysians still uncontactable as checks expand to Nepal–China border areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Fifty-five Malaysians remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides that struck Rasuwa District, Nepal on August 26, according to Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry. “Two Malaysians previously reported as uncontactable have since been contacted, and verification of the remaining cases is ongoing,” the ministry, widely known as Wisma Putra, said in its latest statement updating the situation in Nepal and surrounding areas. The Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu continues to work with the Emergency Response Team of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Nepal, the Nepal Tourism Board, travel agencies and relevant local authorities.

items.title: Nearly RM250,000 payout after Segambut jogger fractures spine while fending off neighbour’s German Shepherds
items.summary: Sinar Harian reported that KL Sessions Court judge Zawiyah Saad found Datuk Seri Ong Thiam Boon liable for the February 10, 2021 incident involving his neighbour, Datuk Mohd Kamal Abdullah. The court awarded Mohd Kamal RM178,457.60 in special damages and RM70,000 in general damages after a full trial. Ong, however, denied that the dogs had attacked or even come into contact with Mohd Kamal.

items.title: BNM warns of scammers using phone numbers similar to STR, Sara hotlines and impersonating MoF officials
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 29 — Members of the public have been advised to remain vigilant against individuals impersonating officials from the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) programmes. Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), in issuing the warning, said some criminal groups had resorted to using telephone numbers similar to official hotlines to contact members of the public and gain their trust before obtaining their personal and banking information. The central bank appealed to the public not to disclose any personal or banking information to unidentified callers, including their MyKad number, bank account number, One-Time Password (OTP) or Transaction Authorisation Code (TAC), online banking password or Personal Identification Number (PIN), and other personal and financial information.

items.title: Pakatan open to Bersatu tie-up for Melaka state election as Amirudin says ‘that is politics’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to working with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia in the coming Melaka state election, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said, signalling that even former political adversaries could become potential partners as parties manoeuvre ahead of the polls. “Bersatu? PAS has also worked with Bersatu, PAS has separated from Bersatu, PAS has separated from Umno, and PAS has wanted to work with Umno.

items.title: Printer apologises, says last-minute order led to incorrect Jalur Gemilang star worn by Kedah MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — A printing company has blamed a rushed last-minute order and less thorough quality checks for an incorrect Jalur Gemilang star appearing on attire worn by Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor and several dignitaries at a Merdeka event. The Ayer Keroh, Melaka-based company said an error during production resulted in the star on the printed Malaysian flag having fewer than the official 14 points. The company said it would immediately provide replacement attire that complied with the official specifications of the Jalur Gemilang.

items.title: Parents must caution teens that mule accounts can lead to legal action, says Ewon
items.summary: Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III Datuk Ewon Benedick, who is also Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport Minister, said allowing others to use their bank accounts could expose account holders to legal action if the accounts were found to have been used for fraud or other unlawful transactions. “Digital technology is now part of our daily lives. Ewon, who is also Penampang Member of Parliament, said digital technology had changed how people carried out various activities, including financial transactions, business dealings and applications for government assistance.

items.title: Amirudin tells Umno to ‘look in the mirror’ over sincerity in election seat talks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — PKR election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has pushed back against Umno’s call for sincerity in future election negotiations, saying Barisan Nasional (BN) should first examine its own approach after Pakatan Harapan (PH) previously gave up seats it had won to accommodate its unity government partner. Utusan Malaysia reported that Amirudin said negotiations would become difficult if one side imposed conditions before discussions had even begun. “Don’t impose conditions before discussions have even begun.

items.title: Desa ParkCity deaths: Post-mortems show two children were stabbed in the neck, mother suffered sharp-force wounds, says KL police chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Two children found dead with their parents at a Desa ParkCity home were killed by stab wounds to the neck, post-mortem examinations have confirmed. Berita Harian reported that Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said their mother, 47, meanwhile, died from sharp-force trauma to the neck and chest. “The post-mortem found that the cause of death was sharp-force trauma to the neck and chest,” Fadil said.

items.title: Putrajaya comes alive as National Day 2026 full rehearsal gets under way
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Dataran Putrajaya came alive with uniformed contingents, Jalur Gemilang and the roar of national assets during today’s full rehearsal for the 2026 National Day celebrations. Beginning at 8 am, the rehearsal provided a preview of Monday’s celebrations, featuring corporate and government-linked companies (GLCs) and colourful special performances. — Bernama pic Among the highlights of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) rehearsal was a human graphic performance involving 1,500 students from 36 schools in Selangor.

items.title: Durian, pineapple and RM8b in deals: Malaysia goes big at MAHA 2026
items.summary: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said about RM4 billion of the total would involve partnerships with China, while the remainder would involve other countries. He said the agreements would cover technology exchange, investment opportunities, capacity building and training for farmers, including Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), as well as creating opportunities for local agri-food products to enter export markets. He added that the MAHA Go Global initiative would also help expand the reach of local products, particularly in Central Asia and Eastern Europe.

items.title: Jendela Phase Two to begin at 1,000 sites nationwide this year, says deputy minister
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 29 — A total of 1,000 sites, including in Sabah and Sarawak, have been identified for the implementation of Phase Two of the National Digital Network (Jendela) plan this year, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching. She said its implementation would ensure stronger and more stable internet coverage nationwide. She said free public transport facilities, including shuttle buses, would also be provided at MRT Putrajaya Sentral every five minutes, while services at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre would operate every 10 minutes.

items.title: More than 2,300 police deployed for National Day celebrations in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — A total of 2,354 members and officers of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have been assigned to ensure the highest level of security and smooth running of the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on Monday. Aidi Sham also reminded the public not to bring any dangerous weapons when attending the National Day celebration. Earlier, Fahmi said the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31, will so far be held as usual, Themed “ Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati ”, the 69th National Day celebration will be held at Dataran Putrajaya with an expectation of more 80,000 visitors coming to witness the historic day.

items.title: Fire destroys 60pc of Pos Laju building in Bekenu, no injuries reported
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — A fire destroyed about 60 per cent of a Pos Laju building in Bekenu, about 47km south-west of Miri in Sarawak, this morning, although no one was injured. The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department’s Operations Centre said in a statement today that it received an emergency call at 8.44am before five firefighters from the Batu Niah Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene. The team, led by Senior Fire Officer II Azalan Azaman, arrived at about 9.30am and found the Pos Laju building, measuring about 15.2m by 12.2m, on fire.
